subject: KiteHealth pilot — confirmation of no-model-training + log minimization
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@kitehealth.com>, KiteHealth Security <security@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: privacy commitments and next steps for KiteHealth pilot

Hi Jared / KiteHealth team —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the actions we agreed on so we have everything in writing: 

Summary of commitments (Redwood -> KiteHealth):
- Training on customer content: Redwood will NOT use KiteHealth ingestion or conversation data to train or improve general models. No model updates will be performed using customer-provided data for the pilot.
- Logging & retention: Diagnostic logs (request metadata, anonymized traces) will be retained for troubleshooting only. Default retention proposed: 30 days.
- PII handling: Redwood will apply automated PII masking on ingestion (names, SSNs, direct identifiers) and provide a pseudonymization option for identifiers that KiteHealth elects to keep for analytics.
- Data residency: Pilot workload will be served from our us-east-1 region; data will not be copied to other regions unless explicitly authorized.
- Access & keys: Customer-managed KMS keys supported; RBAC for log access and audit logging will be enabled.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-data-processing-addendum-v1.pdf (proposed wording for the data processing section) and a link to the MPA template. Please review and confirm whether the 30-day retention and masking approach aligns with your security posture. If you prefer a shorter retention window, let us know — we can accommodate.

Next steps:
1) Jared to confirm opt-out from model training in writing (so we can update the DPA).
2) KiteHealth to indicate desired retention window (14 / 30 / custom).
3) Once confirmed, we’ll circulate an updated DPA and a DocuSign link for signatures.
4) Sergio will stand up the pilot config (region, KMS) once signed.

Thanks — want to make this as low-risk and reversible as possible.

— Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-data-processing-addendum-v1.pdf
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@kitehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: KiteHealth Security <security@kitehealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: privacy commitments and next steps for KiteHealth pilot

Olga — thanks for the concise summary. Confirming on behalf of KiteHealth: 

1) We confirm KiteHealth requests that Redwood NOT use any customer conversation or ingestion data for model training or for any model improvement efforts outside this pilot. This includes aggregated re-training, fine-tuning, or evaluation against KiteHealth data.
2) Regarding retention: security is asking for a 14-day maximum for diagnostic logs that contain transactional metadata. We understand there will be separate, minimal audit logs kept for compliance; please state the difference in the DPA wording.
3) PII: we require automatic PII redaction on any free-text fields that may contain PHI. If pseudonymization is offered, KiteHealth security will review the algorithm and transformation approach before enabling it.

We’ll attach a short security checklist (high level) and our legal lead will expect a revised DPA that reflects the 14-day window and explicit non-training language.

Jared Liu
Head of Product, Platform | KiteHealth
jared.liu@kitehealth.com

--
KiteHealth Security: please advise if we should add any additional constraints to the DPA or if a limited retention exception is possible for specific debugging incidents (with SLA'd deletion requests).
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: privacy commitments and next steps for KiteHealth pilot

Thanks Jared — appreciate the clear direction. Short answers and proposed edits: 

- Non-training language: we will add a clause to the DPA stating: “Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, tune, or otherwise improve model weights or base models used by third parties during the term of the Agreement or for retention periods thereafter without Customer’s prior written consent.”
- Retention: we’ve updated the addendum to reflect a 14-day retention for troubleshooting logs that may contain metadata (request IDs, latency, anonymized headers). We will retain separate immutable audit records for compliance events for up to 90 days (these will not include full request content).
- PII/PHI masking: we will enable automated redaction by default. For pseudonymization, we will provide the transformation spec and a privacy impact summary for your security review before enabling.
- Deletion & emergency access: we’ll accept on-demand deletion requests that trigger expedited removal of content and diagnostic records; SLA for deletion requests will be 48 hours for pilot scope.

I’ve attached an updated addendum (redwood-data-processing-addendum-v1.pdf — now annotated) and the MPA DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/securelink/abc123.

If that aligns, we’ll prepare the final DPA and get the DocuSign to your legal team. Sergio — once signed, please proceed with the us-east-1 pilot deployment and customer-managed KMS key setup.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-data-processing-addendum-v1.pdf (annotated)
From: Maya Rosen <maya@kitehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Liu <jared.liu@kitehealth.com>, KiteHealth Security <security@kitehealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Quick clarifications on residency & deletion APIs

Laura / Olga — quick security clarifications before we sign: 
- Residency: you referenced us-east-1. Can you confirm that backups, snapshots, and any secondary diagnostic indices will also remain in us-east-1 and that no replication to eu-west or other regions is enabled by default?
- Deletion API: is there a programmatic delete endpoint we can call for the production-cutover that supports a request-id and audit trail? We’d prefer to automate deletion requests from our side.
- Export controls & evidence: for compliance we need a log of every deletion action (who/when/request-id). Will Redwood provide a signed audit artifact for each deletion event?

Thanks — these are gating items for our legal/security.

Maya Rosen
Senior Security Engineer | KiteHealth
maya@kitehealth.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rosen <maya@kitehealth.com>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on residency & deletion APIs — implementation plan

Maya — great questions. Confirmations and concrete next steps below: 

- Residency: All customer data for the KiteHealth pilot (including backups and ephemeral indices used for debugging) will be kept in us-east-1. Cross-region replication is disabled by default and will require explicit written approval.
- Deletion API: Redwood exposes a programmatic content deletion endpoint with request-id support and built-in audit metadata. We will provide an example client and a short runbook for automating deletion requests during the pilot.
- Deletion evidence: For every deletion operation we’ll produce an audit artifact that includes request-id, timestamp, operator id (service account), and a signed HMAC that you can verify. Those artifacts can be delivered to an S3 endpoint or pushed to a secure webhook.

Immediate next steps we’ll execute once you confirm in writing: 
1) Laura will confirm the final DPA language (14-day retention / non-training) and send DocuSign.
2) KiteHealth signs MPA/DPA and returns the executed DocuSign.
3) Sergio will provision the pilot in us-east-1 using customer KMS and share the deletion API client and runbook.
4) Olga will schedule a 30-minute kickoff with the KiteHealth security team to demonstrate the deletion flow and audit artifacts.

If that all sounds good, I’ll open the DocuSign and route to our legal for final signature.

— Olga
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Attachments (for signing): kitehealth-mpa-docusign.pdf, redwood-data-processing-addendum-v1.pdf
